questions.question:
Select the option that corrects the error in the given sentence.

She performed bad in the exam.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word "bad" is an adjective, but the sentence requires an adverb to modify the verb "performed".
 
• Adverbs are used to modify verbs, adjectives, or other adverbs. The correct adverb form of "bad" is "badly".
 
• Thus, the correct phrase should be "She performed badly in the exam."

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"She performed **badly** in the exam."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1: "bad" **– "Bad" is an adjective and cannot modify the verb "performed." Therefore, it is incorrect in this context.
 
• **Option 2: "good" **– "Good" is also an adjective and does not correctly modify the verb "performed." It is incorrect.
 
• **Option 3: "goodly" **– "Goodly" is an uncommon and incorrect form of the word "good" and does not fit in this sentence.
 
• **Option 4: "badly" **– "Badly" is the correct adverb form of "bad" and appropriately modifies the verb "performed."

options.text: acts as a landmark for many

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 4**.

__
 
• The error in the sentence lies in the use of "An" before "eucalyptus tree". "Eucalyptus" starts with a vowel sound (the "e" sound), so the correct article to use is "A" instead of "An".
 
• The correct phrase should be "A eucalyptus tree" because the word "eucalyptus" begins with a vowel sound, not a consonant sound.

**Correct Sentence:** *"A eucalyptus tree in my backyard acts as a landmark for many to reach my house."*

He hardness ever / complains about / his workload because / he enjoys his job.

questions.question: Your sibling accidentally broke your favourite vase. Which of the following idioms might you use to tell them not to worry about it?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 1 (Don't cry over spilt milk!)**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The idiom **"Don't cry over spilt milk!"** means that there is no use worrying about something that has already happened and cannot be changed. (जो हुआ है उसे लेकर परेशान होने का कोई फायदा नहीं है।)

 
 
• **Example:** After losing the game, she reminded herself not to cry over spilt milk and focused on preparing for the next match.
 
 
 
• **"Broken Vase"** refers to an item that is physically damaged or shattered. (टूटा हुआ फूलदान)
 
 
• **Example:** The broken vase lay scattered on the floor, but she chose to forgive her sibling and move on.
 
 
 
• Hence, the idiom **"Don't cry over spilt milk!"** is appropriate in this situation as it encourages letting go of minor accidents or mishaps.

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 1 (Don't cry over spilt milk!)**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Shallow brooks are noisy** (छिछले नाले शोर करते हैं): This idiom implies that people with little knowledge often talk the most or make unnecessary noise.

 
 
• **Example:** His constant interruptions proved the saying "shallow brooks are noisy" to be true.
 
 
 
• **Bite the bullet** (मुश्किल को सहन करना): This idiom means to face a painful or unpleasant situation with courage.
 
 
• **Example:** She had to bite the bullet and tell her manager about the mistake she made.
 
 
 
• **You're walking on air** (बहुत खुश होना): This idiom refers to feeling extremely happy or ecstatic.
 
 
• **Example:** After hearing the news of her promotion, she felt like she was walking on air.

questions.question:
Select the option that will correct the underlined part of the given sentence. In case no correction is required, select No correction needed.

Naveen is __as tall as__ Rocky.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sentence "Naveen is as tall as Rocky" is grammatically correct. The phrase "as tall as" is the correct comparison structure to indicate that two subjects are equal in height.
 
• "As tall as" is the correct form to express equality between two things in this context. The other options would change the meaning of the sentence.
 
• Therefore, there is no need for any corrections to the sentence.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"Naveen is as tall as Rocky."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1: "the tallest"** – This would change the meaning of the sentence, implying that Naveen is the tallest person compared to Rocky, which is not the intended comparison of equality.
 
• **Option 2: "taller than"** – This would imply a comparison where Naveen is taller than Rocky, which is different from the intended meaning of equality in height.

• **Example:** The band started sounding the trumpet to announce the arrival of the king.
 
 
 
• **Option 2: The blow of a trumpet** (ट्रम्पेट की आवाज): Refers to the act or sound produced by blowing into a trumpet. It is not appropriate for describing self-praise.
